claims.nodeLabel: NSC 5412, National Security Council Directive on Covert Operations (15 March 1954)
claims.text: The transmittal is signed by James S. Lay, Jr. and states 'The President has this date approved the enclosed National Security Council directive.' Washington, 15 March 1954. Top Secret. The source note places the copy in the Eisenhower Library, Special Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs Records.

claims.nodeLabel: NSC 5412, National Security Council Directive on Covert Operations (15 March 1954)
claims.text: Paragraph 6 carries the deniability test in substantially the words NSC 10/2 used six years earlier: covert operations are to be so planned and executed that 'any U.S. Government responsibility for them is not evident to unauthorized persons and that if uncovered the U.S. Government can plausibly disclaim any responsibility.'

claims.nodeLabel: NSC 5412, National Security Council Directive on Covert Operations (15 March 1954)
claims.text: Paragraph 4 invokes section 102(d)(5) of the National Security Act of 1947 and makes the Director of Central Intelligence responsible for keeping covert operations consistent with United States foreign and military policy, through designated representatives of the Secretaries of State and Defense.

claims.nodeLabel: NSC 5412, National Security Council Directive on Covert Operations (15 March 1954)
claims.text: Paragraph 7 supersedes and rescinds NSC 10/2 and NSC 10/5, and paragraph 7(c) makes the Operations Coordinating Board the normal channel for coordinating support among State, Defense and CIA.

edges.note: Paragraph 7 supersedes and rescinds NSC 10/2 and NSC 10/5. The 1948 charter the board already carries was live for not quite six years.
